teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Seventeen million people paid for a game they couldn't play. GTA VI banked over $1.6 billion first.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: a neon-lit Miami-like street at dusk, a crowd of eager fans holding glowing consoles toward a giant sunset skyline, wide shot, warm pink and teal light.

teile.name: Cost question
teile.text: But what did making it cost? Rumours say US$1–2 billion, and that's unverified.
teile.szene: Original presenter, a blue-eyed man in fedora, grey suit, dark tie and gold pocket watch, stands on a rooftop at dusk, frowning at a glowing city skyline, medium shot, painted open-world-game poster style.

teile.name: Denial
teile.text: Rockstar denied rumours of over US$1.5 billion. It still won't give a figure.
teile.szene: A faceless studio executive silhouette in a dim glass office, hand raised in a firm refusing gesture toward a crowd of reporters with microphones, medium shot, moody painted game-poster lighting.

teile.name: Teams doubled
teile.text: So what's known? Rockstar's teams more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2.
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game scene of a vast studio floor where developers crowd around desks, a Western-themed frontier painting on the wall, presenter in fedora and grey suit watching from a balcony, wide shot, golden light.

teile.name: Growth
teile.text: Staff grew from 2,441 to 4,711. Extra hours earned paid time off or pay.
teile.szene: Painted scene of a bustling modern studio floor filling with more and more developers at desks, a manager handing a relieved developer a coat to go home, medium-wide shot, cool daylight.

teile.name: Payoff
teile.text: Over $1.6 billion came in before launch day; what Rockstar spent remains unverified.
teile.szene: Presenter in fedora, grey suit and gold pocket watch stands before a neon beachside Miami-like plaza at night, crowd of fans with glowing consoles behind him, calm space above and below, medium shot, vivid painted game-poster light.

teile.name: Call to action
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Presenter in fedora, grey suit and gold pocket watch glances at the watch on a sunset Miami-like boulevard, calm space above and below, medium shot, warm painted game-poster light.

belege.name: Grand Theft Auto VI
belege.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a 2026 action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games. It is the eighth main entry in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V, and the sixteenth entry overall. Set within the fictional US state of Leonida, based on Florida, and in the fictional city of Vice City, based on Miami, the story follows the criminal duo of Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Players are able to freely roam Leonida's open world.
Preliminary work began in 2014 following the release of Grand Theft Auto V, with principal production starting after the launch of Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018. Rockstar's global development teams more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. Miami and its surrounding areas were extensively researched for the game's world, which parodies 2020s American culture. The protagonists' dynamic is inspired by the notorious outlaw duo Bonnie and Clyde, and the non-player characters (NPCs) were written to ensure players experience different areas of Vice City.
Following years of speculation and anticipation, Rockstar confirmed in February 2022 that the game was in development. That September, footage from unfinished versions was leaked. Grand Theft Auto VI was formally revealed in December 2023. It became the most preordered video game of all time, with estimated sales exceeding 17 million digital copies, generating over $1.6 billion in revenue prior to launch. Following two delays, further leaks, and an extensive marketing campaign, it was released on 19 November 2026 for the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S to universal critical acclaim. It surpassed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998) to become the highest-rated video game on Metacritic, and it is the only game from the 21st century to achieve an overall score of 99.


== Gameplay ==

Grand Theft Auto VI is a single-player, action-adventure game set within an open world played from a third-person view as either Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos. Players can choose to fight non-player characters (NPCs), steal vehicles, rob establishments or get into high-speed chases with the police. When roaming freely, players have several options for activities such as skydiving, wrestling, basketball, exercising, kayaking and scuba diving.
Throughout the game, players can gain or lose weight—a returning feature from Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas—as both characters, and if the player stays awake as either character for days on end, it will become visible on their faces. The game has a "Criminal Profile" rating system that tracks each player character's reputation based on their actions, similar to the honour system previously used in Red Dead Redemption 2. This system is not meant to portray Lucia and Jason as "do-gooders", but will track whether each character keeps their crimes professional or commits unnecessary violence with in-game consequences that reflect their reputation.
In free roam, as Jason or Lucia, players can choose to split the two up to go and do their own activities independently or stay, hang out and do activities together. Their relationship can depend on the player's actions, and the relationship as a whole is optional. Grand Theft Auto VI features a fully integrated social media app called Snapmatic, returning from Grand Theft Auto V. The app is meant to parody 2020s social media trends and apps such as TikTok and Instagram. Players have the option to customise the appearance of Jason and Lucia, such as changing their hair, clothes and accessories.


== Synopsis ==


=== Setting and characters ===

Grand Theft Auto VI is set within the fictional US state of Leonida, based on Florida; its map is reported to be three times larger than the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2.  The map includes Vice City, Grassrivers, and the Leonida Keys (inspired by Miami, the Everglades, and the Florida Keys, respectively). Additional locations include Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga National Park, and Port Gellhorn. The game world parodies 2020s American culture, with satirical depictions of social media and influencer culture, law enforcement tactics and technology like police body cameras, and references to Internet memes such as Florida Man.
The story follows a criminal couple: Jason Duval, who worked for local drug runners in the Leonida Keys after serving in the Army; and Lucia Caminos (Manni L. Perez), the series' first canon female protagonist, who was imprisoned at Leonida Penitentiary after fighting for her family from Liberty City. Following a failed bank heist, the duo encounters a state-wide conspiracy and are forced to protect each other.
Other characters include: Cal Hampton, Jason's paranoid friend; Boobie Ike, who runs a business empire in Vice City; Dre'Quan Priest, owner of the record label Only Raw Records with Boobie; Bae-Luxe and Roxy, a musical duo signed to Only Raw under the name Real Dimez; Raul Bautista, a seasoned bank robber; and Brian Heder (Stephen Root), a long-time drug runner in the Keys and Jason's landlord.


== Development ==
Rockstar Games began preliminary work on Grand Theft Auto VI in 2014 after its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, was released, with early development starting in late 2018 following the release of Red Dead Redemption 2. Principal production began in 2020, code-named Project Americas. Pre-production on Project Americas began in 2015 with Rockstar initially hoping it would be co-developed alongside Red Dead Redemption 2 whose development was being helmed by Rockstar San Diego. However, as ambition grew for Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar pooled all of its studios together to focus on the title while development on Grand Theft Auto VI was delayed. Rockstar's worldwide development teams more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2's release. When the game released, Rockstar had 2,441 employees which grew to 4,711 across 12 offices during the development of Grand Theft Auto VI. Rockstar wanted to avoid their standard crunch practices that had become prevalent during production on Red Dead Redemption 2, offering staff paid time off if they had worked extra hours or additional pay.
Resources were reallocated from Red Dead Online and planned remasters in 2022 to prioritise development. Rumours and analysts suggested the budget surpassed US$1–2 billion, which would make it the most expensive game ever developed, though the figure remains unverified. Rockstar denied rumours that it cost over US$1.5 billion, though it would not disclose a specific figure. Rockstar requested employees cease remote work and return to offices from April 2024 "for productivity and security" as the release date neared. The Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB) criticised Rockstar for contradicting promises to maintain flexible working conditions; employees were concerned that effects to health and morale could prompt resignations and crunch, especially as managers still maintained flexibility.
